content:
Based on my visual analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Close-up of a soybean petiole/stem at a node
- Brown to dark brown continuous discoloration running along the petiole length
- Green pods visible in background (plant still active)
- Hairy/pubescent stem texture visible
- No white mycelium, no powdery coating, no water-soaked lesions

**Candidate reasoning:**
- **Anthracnose**: Brown irregularly shaped spots on stems/petioles — matches the brown elongated lesion along the petiole
- **Cercospora**: Reddish-purple lesions on petioles — the color is more brown than reddish-purple
- **Diaporthe**: Parallel rows of black pycnidia on stems — doesn't match (no visible pycnidia rows)
- **White Mold**: White fluffy growth — absent here
- **Bacterial Blight**: Water-soaked lesions with yellow halos on leaves — not matching

The brown elongated lesion along the petiole with green pods in the background most closely matches Anthracnose, which characteristically causes brown, irregularly shaped spots on petioles and stems. The Anthracnose reference collage (bottom right) shows a similar pattern of dark brown marking on green tissue at pod/stem areas.
